overview.purpose: Lightweight, robust distributed message queue running entirely natively within PostgreSQL using standard SQL objects, table-driven message storage, SKIP LOCKED concurrency control, and visibility timeout semantics without background daemons or external dependencies.
overview.architectureType: PostgreSQL relational table-backed message queue with MVCC row leasing via SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, visibility timeout expiration, transactional topic-based routing, pg_partman partition management, and trigger-driven throttled NOTIFY publication.
keyDifferentiators: Pure PostgreSQL native implementation: zero external brokers, daemons, or sidecars required; operations execute via standard SQL functions and transactional tables
Native transactional outbox and two-phase atomic commit: message ingestion, dequeuing, and state changes participate in the application's native PostgreSQL ACID transactions

Three distinct FIFO consumption models: standard per-group batch filling (AWS SQS style via read_grouped), fair layered round-robin (read_grouped_rr with group advisory locking), and parallel multi-group head extraction (read_grouped_head)
High-performance partition maintenance and retention: optional integration with pg_partman for automated message table and archive table partitioning by msg_id or enqueued_at/archived_at timestamps
Transactional AMQP topic routing: wildcard topic matching (* and #) with pre-compiled SQL regular expressions executing multi-queue fan-out within a single atomic PostgreSQL transaction
Trigger-based insert notification with unlogged rate-limiting: unlogged throttle table with millisecond interval gating prevents LISTEN/NOTIFY flooding during high-volume ingestion

components.name: Archival & Deletion Engine
stateManaged: Insertions into pgmq.a_<queue_name> with archived_at timestamp

evidence.observation: Executes CTE deleting message from pgmq.q_<name> and inserting returned payload, headers, and metadata into pgmq.a_<name> with archived_at = now() within an atomic statement.
Acquires init_lock advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(123456)) inside a dedicated transaction before executing CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgmq CASCADE to prevent catalog race conditions.

guardConditions: message is not locked by concurrent transaction
transitions.mechanism: pgmq.read CTE with SELECT msg_id FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY msg_id ASC LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED followed by UPDATE setting vt = clock_timestamp() + interval and read_ct = read_ct + 1

evidence.observation: Locks candidate rows using SKIP LOCKED and updates vt, read_ct, and last_read_at atomically.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: WITH cte AS (SELECT msg_id FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY msg_id ASC LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) UPDATE pgmq.q_<queue> m SET last_read_at = clock_timestamp(), vt = clock_timestamp() + $interval, read_ct = read_ct + 1 FROM cte WHERE m.msg_id = cte.msg_id RETURNING ...

transitions.mechanism: pgmq.set_vt(queue_name, msg_id, vt) executes UPDATE pgmq.q_<queue> SET vt = $1 WHERE msg_id = $2 RETURNING ...

evidence.observation: Updates vt timestamp directly without modifying read_ct or enqueued_at, extending consumer exclusive lease.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: UPDATE pgmq.%I SET vt = $1 WHERE msg_id = $2 RETURNING msg_id, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, vt, message, headers;

transitions.event: Visibility Timeout Expiration (Task Stalled / Worker Crash)
guardConditions: message was not deleted or archived
transitions.mechanism: Automatic time progression: vt <= clock_timestamp() makes message eligible for subsequent SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED scans.

evidence.observation: Messages with vt in the past are immediately selected by subsequent pgmq.read calls with incremented read_ct.

transitions.mechanism: pgmq.archive executing atomic CTE: WITH archived AS (DELETE FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE msg_id = $1 RETURNING ...) INSERT INTO pgmq.a_<queue> SELECT ...

evidence.observation: Deletes from active queue table and inserts row into archive table in a single atomic SQL statement.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: WITH archived AS (DELETE FROM pgmq.%I WHERE msg_id = $1 RETURNING msg_id, vt, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, message, headers) INSERT INTO pgmq.%I (msg_id, vt, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, message, headers) SELECT msg_id, vt, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, message, headers FROM archived RETURNING msg_id;

transitions.mechanism: pgmq.delete executes DELETE FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE msg_id = $1 RETURNING msg_id

evidence.observation: Permanently deletes message row from active queue table.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: DELETE FROM pgmq.%I WHERE msg_id = $1 RETURNING msg_id

guardConditions: row locked via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
transitions.mechanism: pgmq.pop executes CTE WITH cte AS (SELECT msg_id FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY msg_id ASC LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) DELETE FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE msg_id IN (SELECT msg_id FROM cte) RETURNING ...

evidence.observation: Combines visible message selection and permanent deletion in a single atomic CTE statement, skipping the active lease state entirely.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: WITH cte AS (SELECT msg_id FROM pgmq.%I WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY msg_id ASC LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) DELETE from pgmq.%I WHERE msg_id IN (select msg_id from cte) RETURNING msg_id, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, vt, message, headers;

transitions.mechanism: Time progression: message was inserted with future vt (e.g. clock_timestamp() + interval); once current time passes vt, it satisfies vt <= clock_timestamp() predicate.

evidence.observation: send() inserts row with vt set to future timestamp; no background daemon needed to transition state.
evidence.luaOrCodeBehavior: INSERT INTO pgmq.%I (vt, message, headers) VALUES ($2, $1, $3) RETURNING msg_id;

invariants.enforcingMechanism: CTE with SELECT msg_id FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY msg_id ASC LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED joined to UPDATE pgmq.q_<queue>.

invariants.atomicStatement: pgmq.archive executes an atomic CTE deleting the message from the active queue table and inserting the returned record into the archive table in a single SQL statement, guaranteeing zero message loss between queue removal and archive persistence.

invariants.enforcingMechanism: filtered_groups CTE checks NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pgmq.q_<queue> m2 WHERE COALESCE(m2.headers->>'x-pgmq-group', '_default_fifo_group') = gp.fifo_key AND m2.vt > clock_timestamp() AND m2.msg_id < gp.min_msg_id).

invariants.enforcingMechanism: selected_messages CTE selects head_msg_id from grouped head messages, filtered by q.vt <= clock_timestamp() with ORDER BY q.msg_id LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Worker Crash or Network Partition during Message Processing causing Active Lease Starvation
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Automatic expiration of visibility timeout: current time exceeds vt (clock_timestamp() > vt).
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: No background sweeper or dead-letter daemon required. Any subsequent consumer calling pgmq.read or pgmq.pop will match vt <= clock_timestamp() and re-lease the message with an incremented read_ct.

sourceEvidence.observation: WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() automatically re-includes abandoned messages in candidate dequeue sets.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Traditional message queues require central heartbeat monitors or lease swept lists that can fail during coordinator partitions.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Utilized PostgreSQL row-level timestamps (vt) and transactional MVCC state to make stalled message recovery purely query-driven.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Consumers must track read_ct and route messages to an application-level dead-letter queue or archive table when read_ct exceeds a maximum threshold (e.g. read_ct > 5).

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Concurrent Queue Extension Initialization Race Violating pg_namespace Unique Constraint
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: PostgreSQL error 23505 (duplicate key value violates unique constraint 'pg_namespace_nspname_index' on pg_namespace) when multiple application instances call PGMQueueExt::init concurrently during service boot.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Acquire explicit transaction-level advisory lock pg_advisory_xact_lock(123456) in init_with_cxn before executing CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgmq CASCADE.

sourceEvidence.observation: Calls crate::util::init_lock(&mut txn) before executing CREATE EXTENSION.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS in PostgreSQL performs non-atomic catalog lookups and insertions that conflict under high concurrency.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added transaction advisory lock init_lock on lock key 123456 before running extension DDL.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Always gate database extension creation and schema migrations behind a global transaction-level advisory lock.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: High-Frequency Enqueue Flooding LISTEN/NOTIFY Channels Exhausting PostgreSQL Notification Queue
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: PostgreSQL NOTIFY queue buffer saturation (8GB limit) or excessive CPU consumption on connected listener sockets under high-throughput batch inserts.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Gated NOTIFY trigger execution behind an unlogged rate-limiting table pgmq.notify_insert_throttle, enforcing a configurable millisecond cooldown (default 250ms).

sourceEvidence.observation: Trigger updates last_notified_at in pgmq.notify_insert_throttle and skips PG_NOTIFY if elapsed time < throttle_interval_ms.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Un-throttled AFTER INSERT triggers emitted one PG_NOTIFY message per inserted row, overwhelming client event loops during batch ingestion.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Implemented unlogged notify_insert_throttle table and conditional trigger logic with enable_notify_insert / update_notify_insert APIs.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Use UNLOGGED throttle tables for transient rate-limiting state and configure client listeners to combine push notifications with polling fallbacks.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Integer Division Underflow in read_with_poll Causing 100% CPU Busy-Wait Spinning
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: read_with_poll using 100% CPU when poll_interval_ms is set to a sub-second interval (< 1000ms).
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Explicitly cast poll_interval_ms to numeric before dividing by 1000 in pg_sleep(poll_interval_ms::numeric / 1000).

sourceEvidence.observation: Executes PERFORM pg_sleep(poll_interval_ms::numeric / 1000) to ensure fractional second sleep intervals.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: In PL/pgSQL, integer division (e.g. 250 / 1000) truncates to integer 0, causing pg_sleep(0) to execute in a zero-delay tight loop.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Always cast integer millisecond parameters to numeric or float before performing unit conversion arithmetic in SQL functions.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Message Column Deserialization Mismatch Across Upgrades Due to RETURNING * Wildcard
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Rust Diesel / SQLx client deserialization errors (column index mismatch or missing fields) after adding headers or last_read_at columns to message tables.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Explicitly enumerate all returned column names in exact order matching message_record type (msg_id, read_ct, enqueued_at, last_read_at, vt, message, headers) across all DML functions.

sourceEvidence.observation: RETURNING clause explicitly names m.msg_id, m.read_ct, m.enqueued_at, m.last_read_at, m.vt, m.message, m.headers.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Using RETURNING * in SQL functions returned columns in underlying physical storage order, breaking client drivers that expect stable ordinal column positions.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Replaced all RETURNING * statements with explicit column lists in read, pop, set_vt, and archive functions.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Never use SELECT * or RETURNING * in public database extension APIs; explicitly name all projected columns.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Race Condition in PGMQueueExt::create Concurrent Execution
historicalEvolution.rootCause: PGMQueueExt::create performed existence check on pgmq.meta without locking, allowing two concurrent processes to both receive Ok(true) and race on table creation.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Wrapped creation check and table creation inside an explicit transaction acquiring pgmq.acquire_queue_lock before checking pgmq.meta.

evidence.observation: Acquires queue lock transaction via acquire_queue_lock_with_cxn before querying pgmq.meta existence.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Race Condition in PGMQueueExt::init Extension Creation
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Concurrent initialization of PGMQ extension across multiple worker threads raised unique constraint violation 23505 on pg_namespace.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added transaction advisory lock init_lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(123456)) before executing CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgmq CASCADE.

evidence.observation: Executes crate::util::init_lock(&mut txn) inside init_with_cxn.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Lateral Subquery Limit Optimization in read_grouped
historicalEvolution.rootCause: read_grouped lateral join scanned and ranked all messages across each message group, degrading query performance on large backlogs.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added LIMIT $1 to the CROSS JOIN LATERAL subquery to restrict message scanning per group to requested batch size qty.

evidence.observation: Appended LIMIT $1 to lateral subquery in available_messages CTE.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Transactional AMQP-Style Topic Routing with Precompiled Regex
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Lack of publish-subscribe and pattern-based fan-out required application code to manually enumerate and send messages to multiple queues.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added pgmq.topic_bindings table with STORED generated column compiled_regex, converting wildcard patterns (* to [^.]+, # to .*) and executing atomic multi-queue fan-out in send_topic / send_batch_topic.

evidence.observation: Stores compiled regex in generated column and scans bindings using index-only pattern matching.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Parallel Multi-Group Head Dequeuing via read_grouped_head
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Standard FIFO dequeuing concentrated batch reads into a single group, limiting horizontal throughput across independent groups.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Introduced read_grouped_head and read_grouped_head_with_poll to extract exactly 1 head message per group across N distinct groups with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

evidence.observation: Aggregates MIN(msg_id) per FIFO group and locks head rows with LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Worker has exclusive ownership of a message during its visibility timeout window.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: If worker execution stalls (e.g. long GC pause, slow HTTP request) for longer than visibility timeout vt, the message becomes visible again in PostgreSQL and a second worker can read it. When the first worker completes, its call to pgmq.delete(queue, msg_id) or pgmq.archive(queue, msg_id) lacks token fencing (it only matches msg_id without checking current vt, worker_id, or read_ct). The stalled worker will successfully delete or archive the row while the second worker is still executing, leading to silent dual execution and race conditions.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: DELETE FROM pgmq.q_<queue> WHERE msg_id = $1 executes unconditionally on msg_id with zero lease token validation.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Partitioned queues scale write and read throughput smoothly across large backlogs.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: When pg_partman creates new partition tables dynamically during message ingestion, PostgreSQL requires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on the parent table pgmq.q_<queue>. Under high concurrent enqueue/dequeue loads, this lock acquisition blocks all concurrent transactions and can trigger lock wait timeouts or deadlocks.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: create_partitioned configures automatic_maintenance on pg_partman parent tables, requiring table lock escalation during partition rollout.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Conditional message filtering in pgmq.read allows high-performance content-based consumption.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: The queue table index is only on vt ASC (q_<queue>_vt_idx). When conditional is passed (e.g. message @> '{"priority": "high"}'), PostgreSQL must perform sequential filter evaluations on JSONB payloads during CTE candidate selection. In queues with millions of visible rows, this causes heavy CPU consumption and slow index scans unless custom partial or GIN indexes are manually added.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: WHERE vt <= clock_timestamp() AND CASE WHEN %L != '{}'::jsonb THEN (message @> %2$L)::integer ELSE 1 END = 1 relies on B-tree vt index without JSONB message indexing.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: purge_queue safely clears a queue within active production workloads.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: purge_queue executes TRUNCATE TABLE pgmq.q_<queue>. TRUNCATE acquires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table, blocking all concurrent transactions (read, send, archive, delete) until the truncate transaction completes.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: EXECUTE format('TRUNCATE TABLE pgmq.%I', qtable) forces table-level ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Insert notifications reliably alert workers of incoming messages in real-time.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: PostgreSQL NOTIFY is an asynchronous, fire-and-forget protocol that does not persist messages. If no worker is currently connected and actively listening via LISTEN, or if a network disconnect occurs, the notification is permanently dropped. Furthermore, pgmq.notify_insert_throttle is an UNLOGGED table whose state is wiped on database restart or failover, resetting all throttle timers.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE pgmq.notify_insert_throttle does not write WAL and PG_NOTIFY does not queue undelivered events.

boundaryConditions: Process stalls, heavy GC pauses, or slow network I/O exceeding visibility timeout vt cause duplicate execution because PGMQ lacks monotonic worker fencing tokens on delete/archive operations.
Dynamic partition creation in pg_partman triggers ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock escalation on parent queue tables, creating latency spikes and transaction queueing under high concurrent write loads.
High-throughput conditional read queries (message @> conditional) without custom GIN indexes degrade to sequential filter evaluations across visible rows, causing CPU saturation.
PostgreSQL NOTIFY buffer limits (8GB shared memory queue) can overflow if high-volume queues are un-throttled or listeners fall behind processing notifications.
TRUNCATE in purge_queue halts all concurrent reader and writer transactions due to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock acquisition.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes consumer task completion time is strictly less than visibility timeout vt; does not provide automatic background lease renewal in client libraries.
Assumes client applications gracefully handle at-least-once duplicate delivery resulting from network partitions, worker crashes, or lease expiration races.
Assumes application code establishes reliable fallback polling mechanisms (read_with_poll) alongside insert notifications (LISTEN/NOTIFY) to handle lost transient notifications.
Assumes database server system clock advances monotonically; clock jumps backward can stall visible message dequeueing or prematurely re-expose in-flight tasks.
acceptedTradeOffs: At-least-once delivery over strict exactly-once: duplicates can occur under worker crash or lease expiration without requiring distributed two-phase commit coordinators across workers.

Relational table storage over in-memory append-only logs: trades extreme raw throughput (e.g. Redis/Kafka) for native PostgreSQL ACID transactions, relational querying, and seamless integration with existing database schemas.

Unlogged throttle state over WAL-logged durability: trades persistence of notification rate-limiting metadata across server restarts for reduced write amplification and zero WAL overhead on high-frequency triggers.
B-tree index on vt over multi-column indexes: keeps write amplification low during message insertion at the expense of requiring custom indexes for heavy JSONB conditional filtering.
TRUNCATE in purge_queue over row-by-row DELETE: accepts short ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock interruption to achieve instantaneous queue clearing without generating massive WAL volume.
